## Design

### 2026-10-11: Today I worked on designing the PCB. First, I got into KiCad and followed the guide to assemble all the parts that would have to go into the circuit board. I set up week 1 care package libraries in Ki

**7.5h**

Today I worked on designing the PCB. First, I got into KiCad and followed the guide to assemble all the parts that would have to go into the circuit board. I set up week 1 care package libraries in KiCad in the seed XIAO smbol lbrary and "imported parts" footprint library I was able to place and connect the whole circuit board and put it into the shape of Starbie so that everything could work correctly and all the circuits could go where they were needed to go. Honestly, I struggled a little bit in that part because I had to overlap. I had to use the blue connectors to overlap the red one so I could go through the lines to make the circuits go through.

I assigned footprints to every part. My current package has a SMD version of the XIAO C3 instead of the DIP shown in the guide, so I used that instead. To be able to get the outline, I imported the Pixel Art Star as a DXF onto Etchcut and placed parts of it to match the guide layout.

Throughout the time of me connecting the circuit board and routing it, I had to jump through the front layer and through multiple layers, the front layer and the back layer, to be able to get each one to connect because there were barriers. Sometimes, with the reds, the red layer would prevent the other conductors from connecting, so I would have to go into the back layer and connect with the blue layer.

I then ran the DRC to make sure I had no errors, and I had no errors besides the two that the guy told me were okay. I added silkscreen text where I just said "turn" things, just to customize my board a little bit, and I exported Gerbers and drill files and uploaded those things to GitHub.
